title: "Surveys"
page-layout: article
---

Surveys are sustained expository work: a treatment of one area built to teach it rather than to settle a single open question. Most are book-length and read front to back. Some are reference works, consulted an entry at a time rather than read through, and the UC Encyclopedia below is one of those; what puts them in the same section is the purpose, teaching a whole area rather than settling one question, not the shape. Where a [paper](/papers/index.qmd) states and argues one precise result, a survey lays out a whole framework or subfield chapter by chapter — definitions, running examples, and worked constructions building on one another — so a reader can come in without the background and leave able to use the material.

Like papers, surveys here are generated (co-authored) with the help of AI, and the same honesty about that applies: a survey is only as good as the definitions and proofs it contains, and every chapter is open to the same scrutiny a paper's single result would get.

## Where this is headed

A survey isn't meant to stay static reading material forever. The plan is for interactive learning content — chapter-by-chapter slides, worked examples, tiered quizzes — to eventually be generated from a survey's own text, not authored separately alongside it. UC for Gamers below is the first candidate for this, but the intent is general: every survey added here is a future source for its own interactive tutorial, kept in sync with the book it's drawn from rather than drifting into a second, hand-maintained artifact.

## Browse

- [UC for Gamers](/surveys/uc-for-gamers/index.qmd) — a rigorous, code-based language for programming and composing UC functionalities, worked through a signature functionality, a global clock, and a bounded-delay network. Links to the compiled PDF and its LaTeX source.
- [UC Encyclopedia](/uc/index.qmd) -- a reference of ideal functionalities for universal composability, in nine dependency layers. Seven entries are filled in, generated from *UC for Gamers*' own LaTeX; the rest are stubs.
